title: State, Memory and Context Over Many Steps
summary: A model remembers nothing between calls except what is in its context, and the context fills up as an agent works. This lesson shows how to budget the window, compress history, keep state outside the transcript, and add long-term memory without drowning the model.
objectives: After this lesson you can distinguish working state, the transcript and long-term memory, and say where each should live
Compute how many steps fit in a context window and the total tokens read over a run
Estimate the savings from summarisation and from pruning old tool results
Use a scratchpad or structured state object so that critical facts survive compaction
Rank long-term memories by relevance and recency and explain the retrieval trade-offs
prerequisites: The cost of a run (quadratic input growth) from [/learn/agents/agent-loop](/learn/agents/agent-loop), and context windows from [/learn/model-foundations/context-and-kv-cache](/learn/model-foundations/context-and-kv-cache). Embeddings and similarity are introduced in [/learn/model-foundations/embeddings](/learn/model-foundations/embeddings).
